title: Vocabulary: One-Word Substitution, Synonyms & Antonyms
why: Vocabulary is the single biggest block of the IPO English paper. In 2022, 5 questions were one-word substitutions and 10 were synonyms/antonyms, so about 15 of 50 questions (30 marks) came straight from word knowledge. These questions take 10–15 seconds each if you know the word, and a root-word toolkit lets you crack most of the ones you have never seen.

lessons.title: How one-word substitution works: crack words with roots
lessons.body:
A one-word substitution question gives you a description ("a person who collects coins") and four words. The examiner almost always puts in **look-alike distractors** from the same family (Numismatist / Philatelist / Cartographer). Two skills beat them:

1. **Know the high-frequency list** (the tables in the next lessons).
2. **Break the word into roots.** Most of these words are Greek or Latin compounds. If you know the pieces, you can build or check the answer.

### Root bank (learn these ~45 pieces)

| Root | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| anthrop- | man, mankind | philanthropist, misanthrope, anthropology |
| phil-, -phile | love | philanthropist, bibliophile, philately |
| mis-, miso- | hate | misanthrope, misogynist, misogamist |
| -gyn- | woman | misogynist, gynaecologist, gynarchy |
| -gam- | marriage | bigamy, monogamy, misogamist |
| -logy / -logist | study of / one who studies | biology, geologist |
| -cide | killing | homicide, genocide, pesticide |
| -cracy / -crat | rule by | democracy, autocrat |
| -archy | rule, government | monarchy, oligarchy, anarchy |
| -phobia | fear | claustrophobia, xenophobia |
| -mania | craze, obsession | kleptomania, pyromania |
| omni- | all | omnipotent, omniscient, omnivore |
| poly- | many | polyglot, polygamy |
| mono- | one | monologue, monogamy, monopoly |
| bi- | two | bilingual, bigamy, bipartisan |
| a-, an- | without, not | atheist, anarchy, anonymous |
| theo- | God | theology, atheist, theocracy |
| auto- | self | autocracy, autobiography |
| bio- | life | biology, biography |
| geo- | earth | geology, geography |
| -graph- | writing, drawing | calligraphy, cartographer |
| chron- | time | chronology, anachronism |
| pseudo- | false | pseudonym |
| -nym | name | pseudonym, anonymous, synonym |
| patri-/pater | father | patricide, patriarchy |
| matri-/mater | mother | matricide, matriarchy |
| fratri-/frater | brother | fratricide, fraternity |
| sorori- | sister | sororicide |
| regi-, rex | king | regicide |
| infant- | baby | infanticide |
| geno- | race, tribe | genocide |
| uxor- | wife | uxoricide |
| pyro- | fire | pyromania, pyrophobia |
| hydro-, aqua- | water | hydrophobia, aquarium |
| acro- | height, top | acrophobia |
| claustro- | closed space | claustrophobia |
| xeno- | foreigner, stranger | xenophobia |
| necro-, thanato- | death, the dead | necrophobia, thanatophobia |
| -vore | eater | carnivore, herbivore |
| -ible / -able | can be ___ | edible, legible |
| in-/im-/il-/ir- | not | illegible, irreparable, impregnable |
| ped- (Greek) | child | paediatrician |
| ped- (Latin) | foot | pedestrian, pedal |
| ortho- | straight, correct | orthopaedist, orthodox |
| -logist / -ician | specialist in a field of study / skilled practitioner | cardiologist, geologist / optician, physician |

> **Method in the exam:** (1) underline the key idea in the description (hate / love / kill / rule / fear / study); (2) find the root for it in the options; (3) check the second root matches (man, woman, king, brother…). Two-root checks eliminate almost every look-alike.

lessons.title: -ologies, -cides and -cracies
lessons.body:
### Study of … (-logy)

| Ancient remains, pre-historic cultures | Archaeology | Origin of words | Etymology |
| Stars' influence on human life | Astrology | Heavenly bodies (science) | Astronomy |
| Plants | Botany | Animals | Zoology |
| Birds | Ornithology | Fish | Ichthyology |
| Fossils | Palaeontology | Earth, rocks | Geology |
| Earthquakes | Seismology | Weather, atmosphere | Meteorology |
| Diseases | Pathology | Poisons | Toxicology |
| Mind and behaviour | Psychology | Society | Sociology |
| God and religion | Theology | Family descent | Genealogy |
| Handwriting | Graphology | Fungi | Mycology |
| Caves | Speleology | Birds' eggs | Oology |

| Coins | Numismatics | Stamps | Philately |
| Population statistics | Demography | Universe as a whole | Cosmology |

> **Look-alikes the examiner loves:** Entomology (insects) vs **Etymology** (words); Astrology (belief) vs **Astronomy** (science); Ornithology (birds) vs **Oology** (eggs); Anthropology (mankind) vs **Archaeology** (ancient remains).

lessons.title: Phobias and manias
lessons.body:
**-phobia = abnormal fear. -mania = abnormal craze/urge.** Know the first root and you have the answer.

### Phobias

| Fear of | Word | Fear of | Word |
|---|---|---|---|
| Heights | Acrophobia | Closed/narrow spaces | Claustrophobia |
| Open or crowded public places | Agoraphobia | Water | Hydrophobia / Aquaphobia |
| Foreigners, strangers | Xenophobia | Darkness, night | Nyctophobia |
| Spiders | Arachnophobia | Dogs | Cynophobia |
| Cats | Ailurophobia | Snakes | Ophidiophobia |
| Fire | Pyrophobia | Death / dead bodies | Thanatophobia / Necrophobia |
| Blood | Haemophobia | Public speaking | Glossophobia |
| Being alone | Monophobia | Light | Photophobia |
| Thunder and lightning | Astraphobia | Flying | Aerophobia |
| Marriage | Gamophobia | Women | Gynophobia |
| Men | Androphobia | Children | Paedophobia |
| Technology | Technophobia | Sleep | Hypnophobia |
| Dirt, germs | Mysophobia | Disease | Nosophobia |
| The number 13 | Triskaidekaphobia | Animals | Zoophobia |
| Birds | Ornithophobia | Insects | Entomophobia |

> Hydrophobia is also the old name for **rabies**, because rabies patients cannot swallow water.

### Manias

| Craze / uncontrollable urge for | Word |
|---|---|
| Stealing (without need) | Kleptomania |
| Setting things on fire | Pyromania |
| Power, delusions of greatness | Megalomania |
| Alcohol | Dipsomania |
| Collecting books | Bibliomania |
| One single idea | Monomania |
| Oneself | Egomania |
| Lying and exaggerating | Mythomania |
| Wealth | Plutomania |
| Counting | Arithmomania |
| Pulling out one's hair | Trichotillomania |
| Wandering / travelling | Dromomania |
| Writing | Graphomania |

> **Memory hooks:** *klepto* = thief (kleptocracy = rule by thieves). *pyro* = fire (pyrotechnics = fireworks). *mega* = great (megalomaniac thinks he is great). *claustro* ≈ "closet". *acro* = top (Acropolis = city on a hill). *agora* = Greek market-place (open crowded space).

lessons.title: Synonyms and antonyms: strategy and high-frequency list
lessons.body:
### The 4-step method

1. **Read the instruction twice.** "Closest in meaning" = synonym, "opposite" = antonym. The examiner nearly always places the opposite among the options as a trap.
2. **Make your own meaning first** ("Frugal = careful with money"), then look at the options.
3. **Use a test sentence.** Put each option in a simple sentence: "He is a ___ man." The right option keeps the sense.
4. **Eliminate sound-alikes.** Distractors often look like the question word (Ephemeral / Ethereal, Eminent / Imminent, Lucid / Lurid). Similar spelling is not similar meaning.

> **Positive/negative filter:** if the word is clearly positive (benevolent), its synonym is positive and its antonym negative. This alone removes two options in many questions.

### High-frequency words (meaning, synonym, antonym)

examples.q:
Choose the one word: "A person who hates mankind."
(a) Philanthropist (b) Misanthrope (c) Misogynist (d) Misogamist
examples.solution:
Key idea: hate + mankind.
hate = mis-/miso-, so (a) Philanthropist (phil = love) is out.
mankind = anthrop-. Misogynist = hate + woman (gyn); Misogamist = hate + marriage (gam).
Only Misanthrope = mis + anthrop.
Answer: (b) Misanthrope
examples.shortcut: Two-root check: the right word must carry BOTH roots of the description.

examples.q:
Choose the one word: "The murder of a king."
(a) Fratricide (b) Homicide (c) Regicide (d) Genocide
examples.solution:
-cide = killing, so all four fit the first root.
Second root: king = reg- (regal, regime).
Fratricide = brother, Homicide = any human, Genocide = a race.
Answer: (c) Regicide

examples.q:
Choose the one word: "One who believes that nothing can be known about the existence of God."
(a) Atheist (b) Agnostic (c) Theist (d) Heretic
examples.solution:
Atheist = denies God exists (a- = without + theos).
Agnostic = a- + gnosis (knowledge): says we cannot KNOW.
Theist believes; a Heretic holds views against official religious teaching.
The description is about knowledge, not denial.
Answer: (b) Agnostic

examples.q:
Choose the word closest in meaning to GREGARIOUS.
(a) Greedy (b) Sociable (c) Aggressive (d) Solitary
examples.solution:
Own meaning first: gregarious = fond of company (Latin grex = flock).
Greedy only sounds similar; Aggressive is unrelated; Solitary is the opposite (trap).
Answer: (b) Sociable

examples.q:
Choose the word opposite in meaning to EPHEMERAL.
(a) Transient (b) Momentary (c) Eternal (d) Ethereal
examples.solution:
Ephemeral = lasting a very short time.
Transient and Momentary are SYNONYMS, placed as traps for students who misread the instruction.
Ethereal (heavenly, delicate) only looks similar.
Opposite of short-lived = everlasting.
Answer: (c) Eternal

examples.q:
Choose the one word: "Government by the old."
(a) Oligarchy (b) Gerontocracy (c) Aristocracy (d) Plutocracy
examples.solution:
geronto- = old man (gerontology = study of old age).
Oligarchy = the few; Aristocracy = nobles; Plutocracy = the rich.
Answer: (b) Gerontocracy

traps: Atheist vs Agnostic: the atheist says "God does not exist"; the agnostic says "we cannot know". Look for the words "believe not" vs "cannot be known".
Emigrant vs Immigrant: E-migrant Exits his own country; I-mmigrant comes Into a new one. The same person is both, depending on the point of view in the sentence.
Look-alike -ologies: Entomology (insects) / Etymology (word origins); Astrology / Astronomy; Ornithology (birds) / Oology (eggs). Read the second root, not just the ending.
Inflammable does NOT mean "not flammable". Inflammable = flammable = easily set on fire. The "in-" here is not negative.
Synonym vs antonym instruction: the opposite word is almost always planted among the options. Circle "closest" or "opposite" before reading options.
Epidemic / Pandemic / Endemic and Contagious / Infectious are near-misses: pandemic crosses countries, endemic stays regularly in one region; contagious spreads by touch.

practice.q: Give one word for: A person who can speak many languages.
practice.explanation: poly = many + glot = tongue. A Linguist studies languages (need not speak many); Bilingual = two languages; Philologist studies the history of languages. Hook: POLY-glot = many tongues, like POLYgon = many angles.

practice.q: Give one word for: A person who collects postage stamps.
practice.explanation: Philately = stamp collecting. Numismatist = coins, Cartographer = maps, Lexicographer = dictionaries. Hook: PHIL-ately, PHILatelist loves (phil) stamps.

practice.q: Give one word for: The killing of one's own brother.
practice.explanation: frater = brother (fraternity = brotherhood). Patricide = father, Regicide = king, Homicide = any human being. Hook: FRATernity is a brotherhood, so FRATricide kills a brother.

practice.q: Give one word for: Government by the wealthy.
practice.explanation: Ploutos = wealth (Pluto, Roman god of the underworld and its riches). Autocracy = one absolute ruler, Theocracy = religious rule, Bureaucracy = rule by officials. Hook: PLUTO kept the gold under the earth, so PLUTOcracy is rule by the rich.

practice.q: Give one word for: An abnormal fear of heights.
practice.explanation: acro = top/height (Acropolis = city on a hill). Claustrophobia = closed spaces, Hydrophobia = water, Agoraphobia = open or crowded public places. Hook: an ACRObat works high up, and ACROphobia is fear of height.

practice.q: Give one word for: A place where bees are kept.
practice.explanation: apis = bee (apiculture = bee-keeping). Aviary = birds (avis = bird), Arsenal = weapons, Granary = grain. Hook: an APIary is for APIS (bees); an AVIary is for AVIan (birds).

practice.q: Give one word for: One who does not believe in the existence of God.
practice.explanation: a- (without) + theos (God) = atheist, who denies God exists. Agnostic says it cannot be known; Theist believes; Pagan follows a non-mainstream or polytheistic religion. Hook: A-THEist = no THEos.

practice.q: Give one word for: Words inscribed on a tombstone.
practice.explanation: epi = upon + taphos = tomb. Epigram = short witty saying; Obituary = death notice in a newspaper; Elegy = poem of mourning. Hook: an EPITAPH sits upon (epi) the grave.

practice.q: Give one word for: Handwriting that cannot be read.
practice.explanation: il- (not) + legible (readable; Latin legere = to read). Ineligible = not qualified, Inaudible = cannot be heard, Incorrigible = cannot be corrected. Hook: LEGible links to LECture, which is reading aloud.

practice.q: Give one word for: An irresistible urge to steal, without any economic need.
practice.explanation: klepto = to steal. Pyromania = setting fires, Megalomania = delusions of power, Dipsomania = craving for alcohol. Hook: KLEPTOcracy is rule by thieves and KLEPTOmania is the urge to steal.

practice.q: Give one word for: The study of the origin and history of words.
practice.explanation: Etymology (etymon = true sense of a word). Entomology = insects (the classic trap), Ethnology = races and cultures, Ecology = organisms and environment. Hook: ENTomology has ANTs; ETYmology has words.

practice.q: Give one word for: One who is present everywhere at the same time.
practice.explanation: omni = all + present. Omnipotent = all-powerful, Omniscient = all-knowing (sci = know, as in science), Omnivorous = eating everything. Hook: POTENT = power, SCIENCE = knowledge, PRESENT = place.

practice.q: Give one word for: A remedy for all diseases or difficulties.
practice.explanation: pan = all + akos = cure. Placebo = a dummy pill; Antidote = counters a specific poison; Vaccine = prevents a specific disease. Hook: PAN means all, as in PANdemic (all people) and PANacea (all cures).

practice.q: Give one word for: A person who remains unmoved by pleasure or pain.
practice.explanation: Stoics (Greek philosophers) taught calm acceptance of both joy and suffering. Cynic distrusts others' motives; Hedonist lives for pleasure; Sceptic doubts claims. Hook: a STOIC stays STILL, whatever happens.

practice.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to FRUGAL.
practice.explanation: Frugal = careful and economical with money. Wasteful is the antonym; Generous is opposite in spirit; Greedy is a different idea (wanting more). Hook: FRUGAL people count every rupee, and so do THRIFTY ones.

practice.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to EPHEMERAL.
practice.explanation: Ephemeral = lasting a very short time (Greek "for a day"). Eternal is the antonym trap; Ethereal (light, heavenly) only looks similar. Hook: an EPHEMERAL mayfly lives one day; it is TRANSIENT.

practice.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to CANDID.
practice.explanation: Candid = honest and direct. Secretive is the opposite; Clever and Polite are unrelated qualities. Hook: a CANDID camera shows the truth, and CANDID speech is FRANK.

practice.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to ALLEVIATE.
practice.explanation: Alleviate = make pain or trouble less severe. Aggravate is the antonym; Elevate and Alienate are sound-alikes. Hook: al-LEVI-ate shares a root with LEVItate, "to lighten"; it lightens the load.

practice.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to OBSTINATE.
practice.explanation: Obstinate = refusing to change one's mind. The three distractors just share the ob- beginning. Hook: an OBSTINATE person puts an OBSTacle in every discussion.

practice.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to MEAGRE.
practice.explanation: Meagre = too little in amount. Abundant is the opposite; Meaningful is a sound-alike. Hook: a MEAGRE meal leaves you MEAGRE-ly (thinly) fed.

practice.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to LOQUACIOUS.
practice.explanation: Loquacious = talking a lot (loqui = to speak). Eloquent means speaking WELL, not speaking MUCH, so it is the trap. Quiet is the antonym. Hook: LOQUacious and eLOQUent share the root "speak"; loquacious is about quantity.

practice.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to EXONERATE.
practice.explanation: Exonerate = declare someone free from blame (ex = out of + onus = burden). Accuse is the opposite. Hook: EX-ONUS, which means the burden of blame is taken off.

practice.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to BENEVOLENT.
practice.explanation: bene = good, male = bad; volent = wishing. Kind, Charitable and Benign are all synonyms. Hook: BENEfit is good and MALice is bad.

practice.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to DILIGENT.
practice.explanation: Diligent = hard-working; opposite = indolent (lazy). Industrious is a synonym trap. Hook: INDOLENT = IN-DOing-nothing.

practice.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to ZENITH.
practice.explanation: Zenith = highest point; Nadir = lowest point. Summit and Apex are synonyms. Hook: Z is at the end of the alphabet, the top of the climb; Nadir is rock bottom.

practice.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to LUCID.
practice.explanation: Lucid = clear and easy to understand (lux = light). Opposite = obscure (unclear). The other three are synonyms. Hook: LUCID has LUX (light), and the opposite is darkness, so obscure.

practice.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to TACITURN.
practice.explanation: Taciturn = saying very little (tacit = silent). Reserved and Silent are synonyms; Moody is unrelated. Hook: TACIT approval is silent approval.

practice.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to WANE.
practice.explanation: Wane = decrease gradually (as the moon after full moon). Its fixed opposite is wax (grow). The other three are synonyms. Hook: the moon WAXES and WANES.

practice.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to COVERT.
practice.explanation: Covert = secret, hidden (think "covered"). Overt = done openly. Hook: COVERT is COVERed, OVERT is OVER the cover and in the open.

practice.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to AUGMENT.
practice.explanation: Augment = increase. Increase and Enlarge are synonyms; Argue is a sound-alike. Hook: AUGMENTED reality ADDS to the real world.
